Subject: Finova: decision criteria (latency / cost / deployment / SLA) - follow-up

Hi Alice 

great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can align with your internal stakeholders.

Call recap (high level):
- Primary use: low-latency inference for customer-facing recommendations + chat.
- Current constraint: P95 latency target + procurement/security gating.
- Key stakeholders: you (product), Rajesh (finance/CFO), security, legal, procurement.

Actions / clarification we need from Finova to put together a formal proposal:
1) Latency targets: please confirm P50/P95 and max cold-start tolerances (example: P95 < 200ms).
2) Cost objectives: target per-inference or monthly run-rate threshold (budget guardrails help us size Dedicated vs Hosted).
3) Preferred deployment mode: Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private/VPC (we recommended Dedicated for strict P95 SLA).
4) SLA and contractual asks: uptime, response times, data residency, SOC2/KMS requirements.
5) Procurement path & economic buyer: confirm who signs and expected timeline.

I attached a short decision_criteria_template.xlsx you can fill for each stakeholder (latency, cost, security, legal). If that makes sense, can you loop in Rajesh and whoever owns procurement/legal?

Next steps I propose:
- You + Rajesh + Legal: confirm criteria in the spreadsheet (deadline: Feb 16).
- Technical deep-dive with Neha/Dylan (30-45m) to validate benchmarks and deployment approach (we can run a short canary test).
- We'll follow with a pricing/options packet once criteria confirmed.

Available slots for technical deep-dive: Feb 11-12 afternoon PDT. I'll send an invite once you confirm a time.

Thanks again 

Marissa

--

Thanks Marissa 

helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Latency targets: our product team is targeting P95 <= 200ms for 1.5k token requests; P50 ideally <= 80ms. Cold-start is tolerated up to 500ms for the first request if warmed after that.
2) Cost objectives: rough internal target is <$0.02 per 1k tokens equivalent (we realize hosted vendors price differently; this is a ballpark).
3) Deployment: open to Dedicated or Private (VPC) if Dedicated can guarantee the latency SLA. Hosted is attractive for speed-to-market but may not meet P95 under peak load.
4) Security/legal: SOC2 is required; we also need KMS integration and control plane separation if we go Private.
5) Procurement/economic buyer: looping in Rajesh (CFO) for budget and signature. He’ll coordinate procurement/legal.

Rajesh 


I’ve added you here; can you confirm procurement timeline? We’re aiming to reach a decision by end of March if possible.

I’ve also attached a quick note with our security asks; legal@finova.com will start an intake if needed.

Best,
Alice
Product Manager, Finova
alice.turner@finova.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Finova: decision criteria (latency / cost / deployment / SLA) - technical notes

Thanks Alice 

great context. Some quick technical clarifications and options based on your targets:

- To meet P95 <= 200ms for 1.5k tokens under production traffic, Dedicated reserved capacity (pinned GPU pool) is the most predictable option. We can design for headroom to keep P95 under 200ms and autoscale for bursts.
- Private (VPC) is feasible; we’ll need to size for your traffic profile and confirm network egress latency. VPC + KMS will meet your security asks but typically requires additional lead time for onboarding (2-4 weeks).
- Hosted can be viable for an initial pilot if you accept a best-effort latency SLO and a canary test to measure real behavior under your workload.

Attachments: latency-sla-options.pdf (short matrix of tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, expected P50/P95 ranges, cost multipliers).

Proposed technical next steps:
1) Short canary test (2-3 days) using representative traffic 


we provide a test harness and sample traces.
2) Dedicated sizing proposal based on expected concurrency and token distribution (we’ll need a 1-week window to size and price).
3) If you prefer VPC, we’ll add network egress validation and KMS key exchange steps to the onboarding plan.

If you confirm you want us to run the canary, Marissa and I can schedule the test for Feb 15-17.

Thanks,
Neha
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
